learningObjective: Map one imbalanced classifier operating point into ROC and precision-recall coordinates and see why the two views create different intuitions.
mediumRationale: Paired deterministic SVG plots provide precise axes, baselines, and synchronized operating points without a plotting dependency. Mermaid cannot express quantitative coordinates.

pages.insight: The deck introduces ROC as a threshold sweep over true-positive and false-positive rates and emphasizes operating-point movement.
The adjacent evaluation slide compares classification metrics and motivates choosing a view based on the failure cost.

deckReview.notes: The deck supplies the threshold-sweep intuition but does not make the imbalance contrast sufficiently concrete. The new paired figure uses one count-consistent operating point in both coordinate systems.

sourceReview.notes: The curves are original illustrative paths. The highlighted point is derived from 10 positives, 1,000 negatives, 8 true positives, and 50 false positives.

agentReview.summary: Recommended paired SVG plots and a synchronized threshold point. Interaction was deferred until a reproducible underlying score dataset can support the full threshold sweep.

implementation.accessibility: Each SVG has its own title and long description. Axis labels, dashed guides, point markers, explicit values, and a count-based caption preserve meaning without color.
